company.name: Toygaroo
company.one_liner: The 'Netflix of toys': a monthly subscription that ships toys to your door.

facts.summary: Parents pay a monthly fee to rent toys, which are shipped to their home, played with, then returned and swapped for new ones.
highlights: Kids get bored of toys quickly; renting saves parents money and clutter.
Toys are cleaned and sanitized between families.
Customers pay a monthly subscription; shipping is included.
The model depends on buying toys cheaply and keeping shipping costs low.

real_deal.summary: Mark Cuban and Kevin O'Leary invested $200,000 for 40% (a $500K valuation).

outcome.headline: Filed for bankruptcy less than a year after the episode.
outcome.story: Demand surged after the show, but shipping and inventory costs swamped the subscription fees. Toygaroo filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in April 2012, and the investment was a total loss.
